subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: During same-process contention, must a synchronous exec decision wait for the in-flight policy write, or may it evaluate the last committed policy snapshot?
rationale: Both choices can avoid the permanent deny wedge, but they define when a policy revocation becomes authoritative; automation cannot choose that exec-authorization boundary safely.

options.title: Read last committed snapshot
options.body: Keep an immutable process-local committed snapshot for same-process synchronous reads, publishing a replacement only after the write transaction succeeds.

options.title: Block until writer completes
options.body: Refactor lock ownership so synchronous decisions remain serialized behind the in-flight writer without blocking the event loop indefinitely.

options.title: Accept lockless file reads
options.body: Explicitly accept stale or fallback-write-visible authorization reads during contention and document the weakened revocation semantics.

recommendation.title: Read last committed snapshot
recommendation.body: Keep an immutable process-local committed snapshot for same-process synchronous reads, publishing a replacement only after the write transaction succeeds.
